behavior: AC1 - the manifest is valid JSON, declares at least one package, has no duplicate source, and every entry carries a non-empty why
verification: bats tests/pi-packages.bats -f 'valid JSON|declared twice|says what it is for'

behavior: AC2 - every declared source is pinned to an explicit version
AC2 - the pin guard itself rejects an unpinned source, so it cannot pass vacuously
AC3 - the packages array is absent from the seed settings.json and neither setup script writes it directly
verification: ! jq -e 'has("packages")' ai/pi/settings.json >/dev/null && bats tests/pi-packages.bats -f 'never writes the packages array'

behavior: AC4 + AC5 - a first run installs every declared package and a second run installs nothing (idempotent)
AC6 - entries present in the live array in the object form are recognised and not reinstalled
AC7 - with pi or npm absent the reconcile warns once and setup continues with exit 0
AC8 - an unreadable or empty manifest is reported, never read as nothing-to-do
AC9 - the Linux reconcile installs through $PI_BIN, not the pi shell function that fails on a locked vault
AC10 - setup-windows.ps1 reconciles the same manifest with the same semantics, adding no non-ASCII
verification: bats tests/pi-packages.bats -f 'setup-windows' && python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if sum(1 for l in open('setup-windows.ps1',encoding='utf-8') if any(ord(c)>126 for c in l)) == 10 else 1)"

behavior: AC11 - a package that is installed and declared is also LOADED: doctor detects a hand-wired extension symlink shadowing it, quarantines it under --fix outside the tree pi auto-discovers, refuses to clobber an earlier quarantine, and leaves an external writer's plain files alone
